compiled_state.title: As a DSO operator, the cycle ledger correctly counts review cycles per distinct PR context for the same commit SHA
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Re-key `cycle_ledger.py` from `commit_sha` alone to `(pr_number, commit_sha)`. Extend `_MARKER_RE_V11` to a v1.2.0 grammar embedding `pr_number`. Provide a migration contract that handles v1.1.0-format ledger entries via the sentinel-pr_number rule (old `commit_sha`-only entries match against any `pr_number` until the next review cycle on each PR re-keys them). Coordinate DefenseStore (TrackerDefenseStore + GitHubPRDefenseStore) re-keying to use the same `(pr_number, commit_sha)` key shape.

**Why**: Without re-keying, the same commit SHA reviewed in different PR contexts (e.g., a sub-PR review followed by a session→main integration review) collides on the cycle counter. Re-key + migrate so each context produces a distinct cycle count and a distinct defense scope.

**Scope**:
- IN: `cycle_ledger.py` schema v1.2.0; `_MARKER_RE_V11` → `_MARKER_RE_V12` grammar; migration contract test (read v1.1.0 entry → emit v1.2.0 entry, no data loss); DefenseStore re-keying coordination; update of the existing `Suppress prior defenses for integration review` step at `ci.yml:523` to operate on the new key shape.
- OUT: Sub-PR workflow file (S1); integration review skip logic (S3); RED-test-blocker required check (S4); runner large-diff aggregation (S7).

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, `cycle_ledger.py` writes entries keyed by `(pr_number, commit_sha)` for new cycles and reads both v1.1.0 (sha-only) and v1.2.0 (pr+sha) formats via the sentinel-pr_number migration rule documented in `dso_ci_review/cycle_ledger.py` docstring.
  ← Satisfies: "The cycle ledger AND DefenseStore are both keyed by (pr_number, commit_sha)"

- When this story is complete, a contract test reads a v1.1.0-format ledger entry, applies the new keying logic, and asserts no data loss in the v1.2.0 emission. The contract test ships in `tests/scripts/test-cycle-ledger-migration.sh` (or equivalent path).
  ← Satisfies: "a contract test reads a v1.1.0 entry and asserts no data loss in v1.2.0 emission"

- When this story is complete, DefenseStore (TrackerDefenseStore via `review-defense-store.sh` and GitHubPRDefenseStore via `review-github-defense-store.sh`) reads and writes defenses keyed by `(pr_number, commit_sha)`. Existing PR-keyed defenses remain readable via the sentinel-pr_number rule.
  ← Satisfies: SC1 (DefenseStore re-keying)

- When this story is complete, the existing `Suppress prior defenses for integration review` step at `ci.yml:523` is updated to filter on the new `(pr_number, commit_sha)` shape — either by filtering on the sub-PR pr_number list, or by reading the ledger to identify which `(pr_number, sha)` pairs were sub-PR-scoped. The filter rewrite ships with a behavioral test exercising sub-PR defense → session→main suppression round trip.
  ← Satisfies: Red team Finding #4

- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic.
  ← Satisfies: TDD Done-of-Done requirement

## Considerations

- [Correctness] The cycle-number derivation in `runner.py:165-168` (`cycles[-1]['cycle_num'] + 1`) MUST be updated to scope to the current `(pr_number, sha)` tuple, not bare sha. Otherwise re-keying causes cycle numbers to fall back to 1 for known-reviewed SHAs.
- [Reliability] PR comment markers from prior cycles (written under v1.1.0 grammar) MUST remain readable by `reconstruct_from_pr_comments`. The v1.2.0 grammar is BACKWARD-COMPATIBLE: it can READ both v1.1.0 and v1.2.0 entries, but WRITES only v1.2.0.
- [Performance] Re-keying touches the hot path of every CI review cycle. Run the existing ledger micro-benchmarks (if present) and assert no >10% throughput regression.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
